question: What is the name of India's first research station located at the International Arctic Research Base Ny-Alesund Svalbard, Norway?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Himadri.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Himadri is **India's first research station** located at the International Arctic Research Base in **Ny-Alesund, Svalbard, Norway.**
 
• The station was** inaugurated in 2008 **and is part of India's efforts to conduct scientific research in the Arctic region.
 
• Himadri conducts research on various subjects, including climate change, glaciology, and biodiversity in the Arctic environment.
 
• Research conducted at Himadri is crucial for studying the impacts of climate change, as the Arctic region is significantly affected by rising temperatures and changing ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Maitri:- **

 
 
• This is **India's second research station**, located in **Antarctica, established in 1989**. It focuses on various scientific studies, including glaciology and meteorology.
 
 
 
• **Bharathi:- **
 
 
• Another Antarctic research station** established in 2012**, Bharathi serves as a base for scientific research in the region.
 
 
 
• **Dakshin Gangotri:-**
 
 
• This was **India's first research station in Antarctica**, established in **1983**, but it has been decommissioned and is no longer operational.
 
 
 
• **India's Polar Research Program:- **
 
 
• India has been actively involved in polar research since the early 1980s, contributing to global scientific efforts to understand climate change and its effects on the environment.
